name: Life Insurance Corporation of India
title: Life Insurance Corporation of India - 543526 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: LIC FY26 net VNB rose 41.63% to ₹14,179 crore, with VNB margin up 360 bps to 21.2% on non-par mix and economic assumptions.
summary.overview: LIC reported record FY26 PAT of ₹57,419 crore (up 19.25% YoY) and net VNB of ₹14,179 crore (up 41.63%), with margin at 21.2% versus 17.6%. Non-par share of individual APE rose to 35.11% from 27.69% a year earlier, and the solvency ratio improved to 2.35 from 2.11. Embedded value grew only 1.58% to ₹7,89,185 crore because of ₹1.00 lakh crore-plus of equity and debt MTM declines in the year. Management flagged upcoming risk-based capital (RBC) rules as the reason it is cautious on dividend payout, even after raising the final dividend to ₹20 per share pre-bonus.

segments.name: Individual business
segments.commentary: Individual APE ₹43,335 crore; non-par APE rose 43.78% to ₹15,214 crore, 35.11% of individual APE. Individual market share fell to 36.6% from 37.46%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group premium ₹1,96,609 crore (+16.26%); group APE ₹23,626 crore. Group market share 70.11% vs 71.19%. Group contributed about 19% of VNB per the Appointed Actuary's breakdown.

segments.name: Bancassurance and alternate channels
segments.commentary: NBP ₹5,076 crore (+45.19%): banks ₹3,151 crore (+22.30%), alternate channels ₹1,925 crore (+109.36%). Share of individual NBP 7.51% vs 5.59%. Policy count fell sharply, which management attributed to a microfinance corporate agency issue.

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: Agency sourced 91.75% of new business premium and 98.42% of policies. Individual agents fell to 14,57,045 from 14,86,851.

guidance_outlook: No formal numeric guidance. Management expects VNB margin to keep improving, driven by higher ticket size and better persistency, but said further expansion will be gradual and slower from here.
Management said it is not looking for major changes in the business mix from here and aims to consolidate, with VNB growth coming from either margin or volume.
Management said maturity outgo will stay high through January 2027 from 25-year-old Jeevan Shree-type assured-benefit policies.
Dividend payout policy will be finalised only after RBC outcomes are clear; management expects the increased payout to be sustained.
April 2026 sales were described as good, ahead of the prior year, across participating and non-participating products.
risks_watch: RBC framework timing and calibration, which is likely to be equity-sensitive and could constrain capital and payout.
Equity and debt MTM volatility: ₹53,698 crore equity and ₹46,853 crore debt fall in FY26 hit EV growth (only +1.58%).
Persistency on a premium basis softened in the 13th and 25th months, and the 61st-month figure fell to 59.31% from 63.12%. The positive persistency variance (₹3,509 crore) may not repeat.
Margin sustainability: the GST charge, RFR tailwind and mix benefit may not recur, and management said margin could be challenged in the next three years.
Agent count down to 14,57,045 from 14,86,851, and bancassurance policy count down about 36%.
Upcoming Ind AS/IFRS transition and its effect on VIF-to-CSM translation, which is still being worked on.
Heavy maturity outgo through January 2027 from high sum assured legacy policies.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth (VNB, margin, PAT, bancassurance), but noticeably cautious on dividend policy and margin outlook, deferring to RBC clarity. Evasive on the FY27 margin level and product-level IRR questions.
key_quotes: We are now very confident that having achieved significant directional changes, we are now on a path of superior growth with sharper focus on enhanced performance parameters.
We do not want to create expectations which cannot be sustainable for future, as a responsible organization, we would like how the RBC pans out.
This journey possibly can be very gradual and slow from here because we have seen even for the industry, the margins have been around between 20s to maximum 30s for a very short period of time.
This is the highest PAT in our history.

qa_highlights.question: Which products drove the non-par individual savings growth in Q4, and how much of that momentum continues into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Uthup Joseph said savings bucket grew about 48.40%, led by Jeevan Utsav on ticket size; Jeevan Labh contributed about 40% of par savings premium. No FY27 momentum figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the VNB margin bridge from 17.6% to 21.2%, and what were the operating assumption and EV walk items?
qa_highlights.answer: A.K. Srivastava: business mix +3%, RFR +3.4%, operating assumption changes including GST -2.8%. EV walk: unwind ₹74,748 crore, operating assumption changes -₹1,663 crore, operating experience variance +₹92,639 crore, equity MTM -₹53,698 crore, debt MTM -₹46,853 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the operating variance positive for several years, and what is the persistency variance breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistency variance +₹3,509 crore, largely from participating and group business; par 13th-month persistency improved (+₹2,463 crore). Group persistency assumption was strengthened. Expense variance positive net of GST; mortality roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the solvency-driven dividend payout cautious even with solvency at 2.35, and how should the payout ratio be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Dinesh Pant said the company wants clarity on RBC because equity exposure is high, and it does not want to create expectations it cannot sustain; growth also consumes capital. Doraiswamy said the payout will depend on regulation, with the increased payout (₹20 per share pre-bonus) expected to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-par IRRs or offering rates be revised in FY27, and why did bancassurance policy count fall about 36%?
qa_highlights.answer: Pant said IRRs depend on investment opportunities, competition and margin balance; hedging for long-duration non-par is limited. Hemant Buch attributed the bancassurance policy decline to one microfinance corporate agency issue and a conscious move to bigger tickets; Q4 sales count rose about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for the next year and the building blocks for expansion from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Pant said margins could be challenged over the next three years and the journey will be gradual; the company will not chase margins at the cost of insurance-for-all. Doraiswamy said ticket size and persistency are the drivers, with product mix to consolidate.

capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning discussion on the call; the call covered insurance sales, margins, capital and dividend.
Capital position: solvency ratio 2.35 at 31 March 2026 vs 2.11 a year earlier; management said it wants to build reserves ahead of risk-based capital (RBC) and that growth will also consume capital.

Digital capacity: 23,00,983 policies completed via the agent-assisted ANANDA app in FY26 vs 14,74,208 in FY25 (+56.08%); active agents on ANANDA up 29.56%. New MyLIC customer app launched (15 April 2026) and LIC Super Sales Saathi app for sales personnel under the DIVE programme.
Bima Sakhi scheme: 3,45,000 Bima Sakhis appointed, 21.94 lakh policies sold and ₹2,848 crore new business premium in FY26; coverage at 1,43,924 of 2,44,876 Gram Panchayats (59%).
demand_pricing: Market share by first-year premium 56.6% in FY26 vs 57.05% in FY25; individual market share 36.6% (vs 37.46%); group 70.11% (vs 71.19%).
Individual new business premium ₹67,676 crore (+8.29%); individual renewal premium ₹2,71,699 crore (+5.91%); group new business premium ₹1,92,912 crore out of group total ₹1,96,609 crore (+16.26%).

Non-par individual APE ₹15,214 crore (+43.78%), 35.11% of individual APE vs 27.69%. Jeevan Utsav was the main contributor to savings growth (management cited ~48.40% savings bucket growth); Jeevan Labh contributed about 40% of par savings premium.

VNB margin bridge 17.6% to 21.2%: business mix +3%, RFR +3.4%, operating assumption changes (expense and persistency realignment plus GST) -2.8%. Individual par ~42% of APE contributes ~28% of VNB; individual non-par ~22.7% of APE contributes ~53% of VNB; remainder group (~19%).

Operating experience variance of ₹92,639 crore; persistency variance +₹3,509 crore (group line strengthened, par 13th-month persistency improved, +₹2,463 crore); mortality roughly flat; expense variance positive, net of GST.

Economic variance: equity MTM fall ₹53,698 crore and debt MTM fall ₹46,853 crore. Bond-amortisation accounting change impact of about ₹11,000 crore gross, of which ~₹9,000 crore sits in participating business (no direct PAT impact per management).

Bancassurance and alternate channels NBP ₹5,076 crore (+45.19%): banks ₹3,151 crore (+22.30%), alternate channels ₹1,925 crore (+109.36%). Policy count via bancassurance fell about 36%; management attributed this to a microfinance corporate agency issue and a conscious move away from login-based low-ticket sales; Q4 policy count reportedly up ~10%.

Agency: individual agents 14,57,045 vs 14,86,851 (down ~30,000); agency sourced 98.42% of policies and 91.75% of new business premium. Management said recruitment, training and younger-age agent focus will follow.

April 2026 sales described as good and ahead of FY26 pace across participating and non-participating products; management said it is too early to judge the effect of recent market volatility on ULIP and guaranteed demand.
Pricing: management said non-par IRRs depend on investment opportunities and competition and are balanced against margins; long-duration hedges are limited. Expense ratio 11.91% (-51 bps).

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management expects VNB margin to improve gradually and says April 2026 sales were good, but gave no capacity additions or quantified orders behind growth. Total premium grew 9.8% in FY26 and market share slipped to 56.6% from 57.05%.
